_note: #1093 R1 + #1111 — set B, VERSIONED WITH THE RULE (13 files: top p1..p9, bottom p1..p4). The programs both jobs post under the one naming rule and the #1111 rule above. vs the 2026-11-07 table: 11 contents identical; the changes are the accepted #1080 deltas (top p7, top p8) and #1111 (top p6 now runs the 25 mm O-flute; the bottom's curved rough joined its pocket program, so 5 programs became 4 and p1 was rewritten — set B's p5 became p4). Goal check identical (98.4 % within 0.01 mm, leftovers 0.90/0.72/0.41 %, cut-into 0); run estimate 2 h 08 → 2 h 21 min, one bit change fewer. The e2e reads this table as the cross-door check.
rule: #1111 (0f comment 6729368477): (a) the canonical owned order — tier (inv: → user: → cat: → built-in), then key — so both doors see one list; (b) the ball tie needs the reach-margin gate (flute − deepest cut ≥ reach.marginMm, recommendation 1.0 mm) while any candidate passes, and a remaining tie falls to the key, printed "by key, pending #1114"; (c) the sequence primary, the curved rough's flat and the rest ball keep their pre-#1111 order under the canonical order, stated as "same diameter: by key, pending #1114" — WITHIN THIS RULE the bottom posts 4 programs (rough + pocket on the 25 mm O-flute) and the top 9. Which cutter among equals a plan SHOULD prefer is the open policy issue #1114 (stiffness vs reach vs bit changes vs time), with three measured plans as evidence.
source: casemaker cut <job>.cutjob.json --location k3-house/location.json, branch 1111-canonical-owned off m1-land13

facedJobCardRename._note: A FACED job’s uploaded names changed with #1093 too: the release store now names programs by the one naming function, as Save all, the sheet and the CLI already did. No set B file is affected (set B has no facing). An operator who cut a faced job from an older build sees the skim’s name change on the card; re-uploading under the new names is the one-time step.
facedJobCardRename.old: <stem>-p1.nc = the skim; <stem>-p2.nc … = the engravings (cut-order numbering, skim included)
facedJobCardRename.new: <stem>-face.nc = the skim; <stem>-p1.nc … = the engravings (numbered among themselves; one engraving = <stem>.nc)
facedJobCardRename.dryRun: <stem>-dry-face.nc for a lifted skim; <stem>-dry-p1.nc … for lifted engravings
